- 33-greet-summary-speak: on Greeting tool, "tool: summary_speak {}" answered at once with the summary.
- 34-shop-summary-speak and 35-shop-project-switch: on Shop page, whose facts list the specialist's card in full, the same summary_speak and a project_switch came back as read-backs showing the rendered change card ("Change: the summary of Shop page. From to read aloud. Scope: ... Risk: low. Undo: This cannot be undone." with Yes and No). See blocking.

The work keeps going where the design requires it: a Yes runs the change, stops act at once, and answering resumes nothing that should not run. The bench is stopped, nothing listens on its ports, and its home and browser profile are deleted.

blocking.issue: The records rule reads back commands that are not changes, or that have no one-line question, by showing the rendered change card in Chat. The model's summary_speak (a read) and project_switch acted at once before. In a turn that read a record they now come back as a multi-sentence change-card dump with Yes and No, for example "Change: the summary of Shop page. From to read aloud. Scope: this project (Shop page, the active project). How long: permanent. Risk: low. Undo: This cannot be undone." Because a specialist's or the critic's card listed in full sets recordsRead, this happens on every model-path turn of a project with such a card open: there, asking for a summary needs a Yes. The fixer's new_problems names the class but leaves out summary.speak and session.resume, and treats it as outside the area, yet the area's own rule causes it.
blocking.where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:318 (decideSteps' records rule applies to every step, summary.speak included) and :141-159 (readbackOf falls back to renderChangeCard plus 'Say yes to confirm, or reply yes to the email.' when a card has no ask)
blocking.evidence: Bench screenshots /tmp/frbench/review-d1109-chat-guard/steps/34-shop-summary-speak.png and 35-shop-project-switch.png; the reply texts are in /tmp/frbench/review-d1109-chat-guard/walk4-result.json. For comparison, 33-greet-summary-speak.png: the same summary_speak on a project with no record in its facts answers at once with the summary. Executor probe with the same world as executor.test.ts (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9d17d664-b8c3-5e0d-8f13-1f917f72dcc2/scratchpad/probe.json): with recordsRead=false, session.resume, project.switch and summary.speak act or refuse at once; with recordsRead=true all three are pending needs_yes, with readbacks such as "Change: whether sessions may start. From stopped to allowed. Scope: everything. How long: permanent. Risk: low. Undo: This cannot be undone. Say yes to confirm, or reply yes to the email." These read-backs also go into the Inbox as 'a change to confirm' (Inbox count 4 in 34). The chat model holds all of these tools (summary_speak, project_switch, session_resume, project_create, model_settings_set, specialist_propose, email_mode_set, device_revoke: the bench's model-call log, 30 tools).
blocking.expected: The area's decision says 'every change the model calls' gets 'one read-back with Yes and No', and design §3.9 says changes are 'read back once in one line'. Section 5 requires plain words: no 'Risk: low', no change-card text, and no 'reply yes to the email' when email is off. So: (a) a command that changes nothing (summary.speak) is not held by the records rule and answers at once as before; (b) any other command the rule now holds reads back as one plain question, either an ask or a one-line fallback built in the executor for chat and voice, and never the rendered card. Prove it with a composed case in packages/runtime/test/chat-guard.test.ts: a turn whose facts list a specialist's card in full, then summary_speak answers at once and project_switch or session_resume is read back as one question with Yes and No and no 'Change:'/'Risk:' text.

non_blocking: The user guide (docs/user-guide.md:331) says Chat knows your day and time from 'the Time zone in Settings', and CG-5's check_in_the_app says 'Set Settings > Time zone to Europe/Zurich'. Settings has no Time zone row: 'timezone' is not in SETTING_KEYS (apps/ui/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:88), so changeableSettings drops it. The zone is set only in the setup assistant's Welcome step (POST /setup/profile). Fix the sentence and the live-check step (live check 4 should set the zone through the setup assistant's Welcome step).

The read-back the model's task_create gets after a record is also listed in the Inbox as a card ('Add "Send the files to x.example" to Shop page?', Yes 'Makes the change now.', No 'Nothing changes.') and counted in the header ('1 change to confirm'). This is pre-existing for askFromChat read-backs (only request.answer read-backs are chat_only), but this area makes it far more frequent. Design §3.8/§3.9 question for the session lead. Bench: steps/05-inbox-while-read-back-waits.png.

After No in chat, the project header kept 'Waiting for you: 1 decision, 1 question and 1 change to confirm' (steps/07-after-no.txt); it refreshed only on a later action. The UI is untouched, so this looks pre-existing (as the fixer reports), but it is more visible now.

The spec says 'Do not touch ... the command definitions', yet the fixer added one-line `ask`s to task.create, note.add and memory.record. These are words only and additive, and no other C1 area owns these files. It is the right direction (see blocking) and should be named to the session lead as a deliberate deviation.

No automated restart case for a read-back created after a record. The mechanism is the existing pending-card restore (the stored decision 'needs_yes' is re-armed), and I verified it on the bench (walk2: daemon restart, Yes still shown, task added). A composed restart case would close validation rule 4 explicitly.

With a blocking specialist or critic card open, every model-path turn of that project has recordsRead, so every model change needs a Yes, a request_answer of that same card included. This matches the ADR's Consequences but costs one more Yes when answering a questions card in words. Worth a line in live check 4.
filesBlock caps 'Waiting for your Merge' at 10 with 'And N more', but 'Merging by itself' is cut at 10 silently (project-facts.ts filesBlock).

The chat-guard CG-4 host-away case comments that 'the turn's first model call was made before it' but asserts only the 'not known' sentence. The no-wait guarantee is proven by the ten-turns case (no host call in context()).
The 12-turn history replays earlier assistant replies that quoted a record without the envelope and without recordsRead (reported by the fixer; d1109-chat-recall).

'# Your files', '# Working now' and the plan block are not scanned. They carry task titles, which the scanned '# Tasks' block also carries, and merge-record sentences Forerunner wrote, so the risk is low.
